findings.finding: The checker loaded the descriptive JSON Schema but did not validate the schema or registry against it.
findings.risk: Schema-required structure, additional-property rejection, and format constraints could diverge from executable conformance.
findings.resolution: The successor checker now validates the schema and registry with Draft 2020-12 and a format checker; a schema-bypass mutation test was added.

findings.finding: Proof 004 and Proof 005 named recomputation checker paths that do not exist at their declared source PR heads.
findings.risk: A portfolio entry could appear recomputation-ready while routing reviewers to nonexistent commands.
findings.resolution: Proof 004 now binds tools/check_ghch_candidate_v0_1.py and Proof 005 now binds tools/check_fork_cad_candidate_v0_1.py; exact-path mutation rejection was added.

findings.finding: Routing-only PR #104 was listed as Proof 001's evidence source and was assigned as serving proposed Proofs 002 through 006 despite not routing those unconstructed proofs.
findings.risk: Routing support could be conflated with evidence provenance or future proof standing.
findings.resolution: Proof 001 now binds its existing proof manifest as source; PR #104 remains routing-only and serves only the currently routed Proof 001.

findings.finding: The candidate checker could accept self-declared proof admission if every gate boolean was flipped true and could accept an active production capability without a separately bound operational authorization record.
findings.risk: Self-asserted booleans could silently substitute for a separate admission or operational authorization act.
findings.resolution: The contract and checker now prohibit candidate self-admission and active production offers; adversarial tests cover all-gates-true and active-offer mutations.
